key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: Engineering stronger transparent-conductor/SAM interfaces targets stress-driven adhesion failure that limits device durability under temperature fluctuations.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide.
Increase surface hydroxyl species to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer (SAM) assembly.
Combine metal–oxygen coordination with cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding for robust anchoring.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85 °C under ISOS-T-3 testing.
watch_item: Thermal-cycle durability is promising, but the abstract does not establish module-scale manufacturability or long-term outdoor reliability.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
